summary: Adam Bowles is an Indology and religious studies scholar who completed his doctorate under Greg Bailey around 2003. He serves as a senior lecturer in Asian Religions at the University of Queensland.
Adam Hardy is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who attended The Royal Grammar School, High Wycombe. He held a post at Cardiff University.

Adam Pearcey is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at SOAS University of London (circa 2017–2021) under Ulrich Pagel, Nathan W. Hill, and Vincent Tournier, alongside training under numerous traditional teachers.
Adelheid Mette was an Indologist who served as a professor at the University of Münster in 1971 and at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich from around 1991 to 1999.
Adeu Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under traditional teachers Khamtrul Rinpoche Dongyud Nyima, Samten Gyatso, and Chögon Rinpoche.

Adolf Friedrich Stenzler studied at Greifswald, Berlin, Bonn, and Paris under Bopp, Schlegel, and Lassen. An Indologist and linguist, he served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Breslau (1833–1887) and sub-librarian at Wrocław University Library (1834–1872).

Adolf Holtzmann the Elder studied under Othmar Frank, Johann Andreas Schmeller, and Eugène Burnouf. Working in Indology and linguistics, he was Professor of German Literature and Sanskrit at Heidelberg University from 1852 to 1870.

Adolf Kaegi was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Rudolf von Roth at the University of Tübingen (1870–1879). He later served as a professor at the University of Zurich from around 1877 to 1914.

Adolf Kirchhoff, a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology, studied at Humboldt University of Berlin from circa 1842 to 1846. He later held posts at Humboldt University and Frederick William University Berlin from around 1865 to 1908.

Adolphe Régnier was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held a post at the Palace of Fontainebleau and served as Professor of Latin Eloquence at the Collège de France from around 1863 to 1884.

Adrian Zenz studied at the University of Auckland and completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger. A scholar of Tibetology and sinology, he held posts at Columbia International University Korntal and the Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation.

Agata Bareja-Starzyńska, a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, conducted research at Oslo under Jens Braarvig and at Bonn. She has held a post at the University of Warsaw since around 1991.

Agathon Benary was a linguist who studied at Göttingen, Halle-Wittenberg, and under Franz Bopp. From around 1833 to 1860, he held positions at the Humboldt University of Berlin and as a professor at the Köllnisches Gymnasium.

Agehananda Bharati studied at the University of Vienna and worked in Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Banaras Hindu, Delhi, Tokyo, Kyoto, and Washington before serving as professor of anthropology at Syracuse University (1961–1991).

Agnieszka Helman-Ważny, a Tibetology and history/archaeology scholar, studied at the Academy of Fine Arts in Warsaw and Nicolaus Copernicus University. She held an affiliation at Cornell University and a post at the University of Warsaw from 2015.

Ahmad Hasan Dani studied under Altekar, Wheeler, and Codrington at Banaras and London. In archaeology and Indology, he held posts at Dhaka, SOAS, Peshawar as archaeology department head, and Quaid-i-Azam University as Dean of Arts.

Ajahn Amaro, a Buddhist studies figure, studied at Bedford College and under Ajahn Chah and Ajahn Sumedho. He co-founded and served as co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery (1996–2010) and became abbot of Amaravati Buddhist Monastery in 2010.
Ajahn Brahm is a Buddhist and religious studies figure who was educated at Latymer Upper School and Emmanuel College, Cambridge (circa 1969–1972). He also studied under Boonman Poonyathiro.
Ajahn Sucitto, a Buddhist and religious studies figure, studied under Ajahn Sumedho around 1978. He served as abbot of Chithurst Buddhist Monastery from around 1992 to 2014.
Ajahn Sumedho is a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied under Ajahn Chah from around 1967 to 1977. He founded Chithurst Buddhist Monastery.
